newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska's new CEO eyes global expansion.
newsitem.headline: Skanska's new CEO eyes global expansion.

text.p: Swedish construction company Skanska AB will continue to invest in international expansion, the company's new chief executive Claes Bjork said on Monday.
"We must think in even more global terms than we do today," said Bjork, currently head of Skanska's U.S. operations, who is to take over from Melker Schorling from August 1.
"The U.S. is a very big market and we still are small but there is also a lot to be done on other markets.
"Skanska's growth will take place outside Sweden," Bjork told a news conference.
Schorling is to take the chairmanship at Skanska, replacing Percy Barnevik who is leaving the board and joining Investor, the investment vehicle of the powerful Wallenberg family, as chairman.
Bjork said he had not yet thought through his exact strategy for Skanska.
"I was asked by Melker Schorling last Monday and accepted the offer the same day," Bjork said.
Bjork, 51, has been with Skanska since 1967, most recently as head of U.S. operations based in New York.
